findings.title: A refresh or tab close while the POST is in flight is never recorded as uncertain, so later definitive-refusal copy can be false and the frozen stamp is released
findings.claim: The pre-POST persistence at AssistedOrderPage.tsx:805-815@7a2bf753 writes acceptedAt but attemptState from the closure ('none'); 'uncertain' is set only inside the catch (:853-861). If the page is refreshed, backgrounded to death, or closed while submitAssistedOrder is pending, the committed-or-not outcome is unknown yet the restored draft reads attemptState 'none' (draft-store.ts:159-160), so no RESTORED_UNCERTAIN_NOTICE is shown (:408-410), and the next definitive refusal (drift :869-871, 400/403/unknown-4xx :887-889) tells the customer 'so nothing was submitted' (:193) or 'was not accepted and was not saved' (:899) and sets acceptedAt to null. The following submit stamps a new acceptedAt (:804), the server fingerprint no longer matches (service.ts:495-510), and the customer ends in idempotency_conflict with no confirmation, routed to support. No duplicate is created because the key is never rotated, but the copy is untrue for a committed request and the replay is lost.

findings.fix: In the pre-POST store call (:807-814) persist an uncertainty marker, e.g. attemptState 'in_flight' that readAssistedOrderDraft maps to 'uncertain' on restore (draft-store.ts:159-160), and downgrade it to 'none' only when a definitive refusal is observed in the same page session before any uncertain outcome; keep the existing 'uncertain' promotion in the catch. Add a vitest case: deferred submit, unmount while pending, render again, expect the restored notice and that the retry carries the same key and acceptedAt and that a subsequent 400 does not release the stamp.

findings.title: The 403-after-uncertain copy promises a same-request retry that the Early Access storage sweep makes impossible; following it can create a second durable order
findings.claim: After an uncertain attempt, a 403 forbidden now says 'Your Early Access session ended. Unlock Early Access again, then retry this same request; do not start a new one.' (AssistedOrderPage.tsx:895@7a2bf753). Unlocking goes through EarlyAccessRoute.readSession, which on an expired or definitively unauthenticated session calls resetCustomerContext (:194, :220, :277) -> clearEarlyAccessCustomerStorage (:102-108) -> clearAssistedOrderStorage (:107), which removes every xenios.assisted-order.* key including draft.v1 (storage.ts:161-195, draft-store.ts:29). The wizard then remounts with no draft: a fresh idempotencyKey (:377-379), acceptedAt null, attemptState 'none', no notice. A customer who does as told re-enters the request and submits under a new key and a fresh session identity; if the uncertain attempt had committed, this is a second durable order. The sweep is deliberate shared-machine hygiene and the same wipe existed at 79414143, so this is not a regression, but the new copy actively directs the customer into it.
findings.evidence: AssistedOrderPage.tsx:893-896@7a2bf753; EarlyAccessRoute.tsx:102-108, :151-161, :194, :220, :277, :394@7a2bf753 (unchanged protected file); storage.ts:161-195; draft-store.ts:29; service.ts:376-378 (email+key hash is per request, so a new key is a new row). Preserving the draft across the expiry sweep would need a protected-path change in EarlyAccessRoute.tsx and a shared-machine decision, and is out of this fix's scope.
